articles.title: Anthropic Releases Claude 4 with Extended Reasoning and 2M Token Context
articles.summary: Anthropic officially launched Claude 4 today, featuring a 2 million token context window and a new 'deep reasoning' mode that outperforms competitors on mathematical and scientific benchmarks. The model introduces native tool use with persistent memory across sessions, marking a significant leap in agentic capabilities. Early enterprise customers report 40% improvements in complex document analysis tasks compared to Claude 3.7.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's AlphaFold 4 Predicts RNA-Protein Interactions at Atomic Scale
articles.summary: Google DeepMind published research in Nature detailing AlphaFold 4's ability to model complex RNA-protein interactions with near-experimental accuracy, a capability that eluded previous versions. The breakthrough could accelerate drug discovery for diseases where RNA plays a central regulatory role, including several cancers and neurological disorders. Researchers at three independent labs have already confirmed the predictions using cryo-EM imaging.

articles.title: OpenAI's GPT-5 Agent Framework Now Available to All Developers
articles.summary: OpenAI opened its GPT-5 Agents API to all tier-1 developers after a six-week private beta, enabling the creation of long-running autonomous agents that can browse the web, write and execute code, and manage files without human intervention. The framework includes a new 'guardrail orchestration' layer that monitors agent behavior in real time and flags potential safety violations. Pricing starts at $0.008 per 1,000 agent steps, drawing debate about cost-efficiency for complex workflows.

articles.title: EU AI Act Enforcement Body Issues First Major Fine to Meta Over Llama 5 Training Data
articles.summary: The newly operational EU AI Office levied a €230 million fine against Meta, alleging the company used copyrighted European publications to train Llama 5 without adequate licensing or opt-out mechanisms. Meta called the ruling 'legally unfounded' and announced plans to appeal, while open-source advocacy groups warned the decision could chill future open-weight model releases in Europe. The case is being watched closely as a precedent for how the AI Act's training data provisions will be enforced.

articles.title: Microsoft Copilot Studio Gains Real-Time RAG Over Enterprise SharePoint and Teams Data
articles.summary: Microsoft announced a major update to Copilot Studio that enables real-time retrieval-augmented generation directly over live SharePoint libraries and Teams conversation history, eliminating the need to pre-index documents. The feature uses a new differential indexing engine that updates vector embeddings within seconds of document edits, ensuring answers are always current. The update is rolling out to Microsoft 365 E3 and E5 subscribers beginning this week.

articles.title: Stanford HAI Report Warns of 'Alignment Tax' as Safety Measures Slow Frontier Models
articles.summary: A comprehensive report from Stanford's Human-Centered AI Institute found that leading labs are spending up to 35% of compute during post-training on alignment and safety fine-tuning, a cost the authors term the 'alignment tax.' While acknowledging the necessity of safety measures, the report urges investment in more efficient alignment techniques to avoid competitive disadvantages against less safety-conscious developers. The findings are expected to inform upcoming U.S. congressional hearings on AI competitiveness scheduled for next month.

articles.title: Runway Gen-4 Video Model Achieves Photorealistic 4K Output at 60fps
articles.summary: Runway released Gen-4, its latest video generation model, capable of producing photorealistic 4K footage at 60 frames per second from text or image prompts with clips up to 30 seconds long. The model demonstrates significantly improved temporal consistency and physics simulation, with water, smoke, and cloth behaving in visually convincing ways for the first time in an accessible consumer tool. Hollywood studios including two major production houses have already announced Gen-4 integration into pre-visualization pipelines.

articles.title: MIT Researchers Demonstrate LLM Self-Correction Without Human Feedback Using Debate Protocol
articles.summary: MIT CSAIL published a paper showing that large language models can reliably identify and correct their own factual errors through a structured multi-agent debate protocol, achieving a 67% reduction in hallucinations on standardized benchmarks without any human-labeled correction data. The technique involves two model instances arguing opposing interpretations of a claim, with a third acting as adjudicator, all running on the same base weights. The authors suggest the method could substantially reduce dependence on expensive human feedback loops in RLHF pipelines.
